Queries._comment: Every hand-written SQL statement the API runs, keyed by Section:Key and read via IQueryStore (see Repository/QueryStore.cs). {Token} placeholders are structural SQL fragments (table/view name, an optional WHERE/AND clause, an ORDER BY) substituted in C# before the string reaches Dapper - never user input. Actual values always stay real Dapper @parameters. Edits here take effect without a rebuild (reloadOnChange is on in Program.cs).

CustomerEnquiry._comment: Standalone contact/enquiry CRUD screen, now branded 'Sale' in the UI (see Database/create_customer_enquiries_table.sql + Database/add_sale_pipeline_fields.sql) - sourced from the client's 'Arun Customer Database.xls' spreadsheet, not linked to automation_records/finance_view/purchase_view (Sale has no reminder/rule-matching automation the other categories do). Pure CRUD only, no email/WhatsApp send logic touches this table. Every query that returns a row explicitly aliases every snake_case column to its PascalCase CustomerEnquiry.cs property name (id AS "Id", contact_name AS "ContactName", etc.) instead of 'SELECT *'/'RETURNING *' - Dapper's default column->property mapping is exact-name-only (case-insensitive, but it does NOT strip underscores unless Dapper.DefaultTypeMap.MatchNamesWithUnderscores is set globally, which this app never does). Without the aliases, single-word columns like phone/email happened to bind fine but every underscored column (contact_name, customer_name, mailing_street/city/state/zip, enquiry_status, is_active, created_at/by, updated_at/by) silently came back null on every read - not caught until the bulk import populated the grid with enough rows to notice every Name/Customer Name/Mailing cell was blank. The Sale Management list page reads through GET api/Inquiry?category=customerenquiry (InquiryController.cs, fn_get_customer_enquiry_records) instead of a query in this section - this section's own List query (with its @EnquiryStatus/@Stage/@IsActive/@Search/branch-entitlement filtering) was removed as dead once that migration landed; GetById/Insert/Update/SetActive/GetExistingKeys below are still the live single-row CRUD path.

InboundMessages._comment: Shared by InboundEmailBackgroundService and WhatsAppInboundService (both retired-n8n replacements) - same fn_match_inbound_message() call n8n's 'Match To Record'/'Match To Record1' nodes made.

InboundEmail._comment: Native replacement for the retired n8n 'WF: Inbound Email (Reply Capture)' workflow (Gmail Trigger -> Normalize Email Reply -> Insert Inbound Message -> Match To Record). See SmartWorker/BackgroundServices/InboundEmailBackgroundService.cs. Insert used to gate on 'WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM automation_records WHERE email_thread_id = @InReplyToId)' - automation_records.email_thread_id is never populated (EmailService.cs sends via plain SMTP, which has no Gmail thread id to hand back; both ReminderSendBackgroundService and NotificationsService.SendPendingNotificationAsync always pass EmailThreadId = null), so that gate silently dropped every inbound email reply before fn_match_inbound_message() ever saw it. Now inserts unconditionally, same as WhatsAppCapture:InsertInboundMessage - dedup is still just ON CONFLICT. fn_match_inbound_message() needs the row to already exist (it looks it up by id), so InboundEmailBackgroundService.ProcessMessageAsync runs Insert + InboundMessages:MatchToRecord inside a single DB transaction and rolls the whole thing back when nothing matched (promo/newsletter mail landing in the same inbox) - so an unmatched message never actually lands in inbound_messages, it's only ever visible within that in-flight transaction, not to any other query.
InboundEmail.Insert:
INSERT INTO inbound_messages
  (channel, external_id, in_reply_to_id, from_email, subject, body_text, raw, is_auto_reply)
VALUES
  ('email', @ExternalId, @InReplyToId, @FromEmail, @Subject, @BodyText, @Raw::jsonb, @IsAutoReply)
ON CONFLICT (channel, external_id) WHERE external_id IS NOT NULL
DO NOTHING
RETURNING id

WhatsAppCapture._comment: Native replacement for the retired n8n 'WF: Reply Capture WhatsApp (Sub-workflow)' workflow's active nodes (Normalize WhatsApp Event -> Is Delivery Status? -> Store + Reconcile Delivery Status / Insert Inbound Message1 -> Match To Record1). See SmartWorker/Controllers/WhatsAppWebhookController.cs and Services/WhatsAppInboundService.cs. InsertStatusEventAndReconcile calls the targeted, single-wamid fn_reconcile_whatsapp_status_for_wamid (see Database/fix_whatsapp_status_reconcile.sql) rather than the full-sweep fn_reconcile_whatsapp_status - a single incoming status webhook shouldn't trigger a re-scan of every pending event across every message. The full sweep still runs on its own via ReminderSend:Reconcile and WhatsAppReconcile:Reconcile, which need to catch anything this targeted call might miss (e.g. an event whose automation_records row doesn't exist yet). DetectConflict is Phase 2 of the interactive-button plan (see Database/add_button_conflict_detection.sql) - called from ProcessMessageAsync right after MatchToRecord, only when message_type is 'button'/'list'. Writes to reply_intents (same queue ReplyClassificationService already uses) when 2+ taps share the same in_reply_to_id, so a conflicting record surfaces in Human Approval instead of an auto-apply silently picking whichever tap landed last. EnqueueRoutedIntent is Phase 3 (see Database/add_button_routing.sql) - called only when DetectConflict returned 'no_conflict' (a single, clean tap), with @Intent/@PromisedDate/@Auto decided by WhatsAppInboundService.ButtonRoutingTable (the fixed action-key lookup, currently Group B/Purchase-delivery only - see the migration file for why the other 3 groups aren't in it yet). @Auto=true immediately applies via the same fn_apply_reply_intent_by_record Finance approvals already use; @Auto=false just queues it the same way Phase 2's conflicts do, for a human to approve.
WhatsAppCapture.InsertInboundMessage:
INSERT INTO inbound_messages
  (channel, external_id, in_reply_to_id, from_phone, body_text, message_type, selected_option_id, received_at, raw, is_auto_reply)
VALUES
  ('whatsapp', @ExternalId, @InReplyToId, @FromPhone, @BodyText, @MessageType, @SelectedOptionId, to_timestamp(@Timestamp::bigint), @Raw::jsonb, false)
ON CONFLICT (channel, external_id) WHERE external_id IS NOT NULL
DO NOTHING
RETURNING id

ReplyReview._comment: Apply and ApplyByRecord call two different functions on purpose, despite the similar names - Apply is keyed by @ReplyIntentId (ReplyReviewService.ApproveAsync only has that on hand) so it must call fn_apply_reply_intent(p_reply_intent_id, ...), which looks a row up by its own id. Fixed 2026-08-14: this previously called fn_apply_reply_intent_by_record(@ReplyIntentId, false) instead - that function's first parameter is p_matched_record_id, not a reply_intent id, so it was either silently no-op'ing ('not_found', whenever no record happened to share that id) or, worse, applying a completely unrelated record's pending reply whenever a numeric collision occurred. ApplyByRecord is correctly keyed by @p_matched_record_id (the Human Approval table's Edit-dialog Save only has the record id, not a reply_intent_id - see ReplyReviewController's doc comment on that endpoint), so it correctly keeps calling fn_apply_reply_intent_by_record, which looks up whichever reply_intents row for that record is currently in human_approval. RecordsInReview's LEFT JOIN LATERAL (added for Phase 5 of the WhatsApp interactive-button plan, reply-review-list.component.ts) exposes reply_intent_id/reply_intent so the UI can show *why* a record is in review (a Phase 2 conflict, a Phase 3 approval-routed button tap, an AI-classified intent) instead of just that it is - LATERAL + ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 guarantees exactly one joined row per record even if more than one human_approval reply_intents row briefly coexists for it, picking the same 'newest wins' row fn_apply_reply_intent_by_record itself would apply, so the badge the reviewer sees always matches what Approve would actually do.

ReplyReview.RecordsInReview:
SELECT v.*, ri.id AS reply_intent_id, ri.intent AS reply_intent,
    ri.promised_date AS reply_promised_date, ri.promised_amount AS reply_promised_amount
FROM {ViewName} v
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT id, intent, promised_date, promised_amount
  FROM reply_intents
  WHERE matched_record_id = v.id
    AND status_id = (SELECT id FROM reply_status WHERE status_name = 'human_approval')
  ORDER BY id DESC
  LIMIT 1
) ri ON true
WHERE v.id IN (
  SELECT DISTINCT matched_record_id
  FROM reply_intents
  WHERE matched_record_id IS NOT NULL
    AND status_id = (SELECT id FROM reply_status WHERE status_name = 'human_approval')
)

Dashboard.RecordJourney:
SELECT 'reminder'::text AS event_type,
    n.sent_at AS event_time,
    n.rule_name AS rule_name,
    n.email_status AS email_status,
    n.whatsapp_status AS whatsapp_status,
    n.email_subject AS email_subject,
    n.email_body AS email_body,
    COALESCE(
        (CASE WHEN n.whatsapp_body IS NOT NULL AND n.whatsapp_body <> '' THEN n.whatsapp_body::jsonb ELSE NULL END) #>> '{template,components,0,parameters,1,text}',
        (CASE WHEN n.whatsapp_body IS NOT NULL AND n.whatsapp_body <> '' THEN n.whatsapp_body::jsonb ELSE NULL END) #>> '{text,body}'
    ) AS whatsapp_text,
    NULL::text AS channel,
    NULL::text AS from_contact,
    NULL::text AS body_text,
    NULL::text AS intent,
    NULL::text AS applied_via,
    NULL::date AS promised_date,
    NULL::numeric AS promised_amount
FROM notification_log n
JOIN {ViewName} v ON v.id = n.record_id
WHERE n.record_id = @RecordId


UNION ALL

SELECT 'reply'::text AS event_type,
    m.received_at AS event_time,
    NULL::text AS rule_name,
    NULL::text AS email_status,
    NULL::text AS whatsapp_status,
    NULL::text AS email_subject,
    NULL::text AS email_body,
    NULL::text AS whatsapp_text,
    m.channel AS channel,
    COALESCE(m.from_phone, m.from_email) AS from_contact,
    regexp_replace(m.body_text, '(On .*wrote:.*)', '', 'gs') AS body_text,
    NULL::text AS intent,
    NULL::text AS applied_via,
    NULL::date AS promised_date,
    NULL::numeric AS promised_amount
FROM inbound_messages m
JOIN {ViewName} v ON v.id = m.matched_record_id
WHERE m.matched_record_id = @RecordId
    AND m.processing_status = 'matched' AND m.is_auto_reply = false
 

UNION ALL

SELECT 'system_action'::text AS event_type,
    ri.applied_at AS event_time,
    NULL::text AS rule_name,
    NULL::text AS email_status,
    NULL::text AS whatsapp_status,
    NULL::text AS email_subject,
    NULL::text AS email_body,
    NULL::text AS whatsapp_text,
    NULL::text AS channel,
    NULL::text AS from_contact,
    NULL::text AS body_text,
    ri.intent AS intent,
    rs.status_name AS applied_via,
    ri.promised_date AS promised_date,
    ri.promised_amount AS promised_amount
FROM reply_intents ri
JOIN reply_status rs ON rs.id = ri.status_id
JOIN {ViewName} v ON v.id = ri.matched_record_id
WHERE ri.matched_record_id = @RecordId
    AND ri.applied = true

ORDER BY event_time

Configuration._getManualRule_comment: Every Journey panel manual WhatsApp send (SendCustomWhatsAppAsync) is attributed to ONE real rule_alert_configuration row per category, instead of a hardcoded 'Manual message' string - no rule picker in the UI. The row itself is pre-seeded per category by Database/insert_manual_custom_rules.sql (rule_name='Custom', alert_type='Manual', whatsapp_template_id set to that category's generic 2-parameter Meta template), NOT created here - this is a plain lookup. Finance/Purchase/Inventory are then repointed to their OWN dedicated template (WA_FINANCE_CUSTOM_NOTICE/WA_PURCHASE_CUSTOM_UPDATE/WA_INVENTORY_CUSTOM_ALERT) by Database/insert_manual_whatsapp_templates.sql, run after the first script - same underlying Meta template_name either way, just a distinct whatsapp_template_config row so it's identifiable as 'the manual-send one'. LOWER() on both sides because the frontend passes the lowercase category key (finance/purchase/...) while rule_alert_configuration.category_name is stored capitalized (Finance/Purchase/...). Joins in whatsapp_template_config so SendCustomWhatsAppAsync can send via Meta's pre-approved TEMPLATE format (bypassing the 24h customer-service-window restriction free-text 'type: text' sends are subject to) - see whatsapp_template_config.body_params for the shape every category's generic template expects: components[0].parameters = [{recipient name}, {{ message_body }}]. This is a read-only lookup - nothing in the manual-send path writes back to rule_alert_configuration; the row's whatsapp_message_body_template is not touched per send.
Configuration.GetManualRule: SELECT r.id, r.rule_name, w.template_name, w.language_code FROM rule_alert_configuration r LEFT JOIN whatsapp_template_config w ON w.id = r.whatsapp_template_id AND w.is_active WHERE LOWER(r.category_name) = LOWER(@CategoryName) AND r.alert_type = 'Manual' AND r.is_active ORDER BY r.id LIMIT 1

Automation._comment: Native replacement for the retired n8n 'WF: Daily Refresh Automation Records (5AM)' workflow - see SmartWorker/BackgroundServices/DailyAutomationRefreshService.cs, which runs this on an in-process 5:00 AM IST schedule instead of n8n's Schedule Trigger.

ReplyClassification._comment: Native replacement for the retired n8n 'WF: Reply Processor (Classify)' workflow's active/published version (Schedule (60 sec)1 -> Fetch Unclassified1 -> Build Prompt1 -> OpenAI Classify1 -> Parse & Validate1 -> Insert Reply Intent1 -> Supersede Older1 -> Notify Approvals (by user)1 -> push chain). See SmartWorker/BackgroundServices/ReplyClassificationBackgroundService.cs. UpsertIntent is the same INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (inbound_message_id) DO UPDATE as n8n's hand-escaped multi-row statement, just parameterized and run once per reply instead of built as one big string. status_id is always 'human_approval' here, matching the currently active workflow exactly - the older fn_route_pending(0.85) auto-apply step exists in the DB but is NOT wired into the active n8n flow, so it's deliberately not called here either. FetchUnclassified's message_type/raw->>'type' exclusion is Phase 1's originally-planned button-exclusion filter (see whatsapp-buttons-complete-plan.html Phase 1) - without it, a button/list tap with no reply_intents row yet (e.g. a lone tap that Phase 2's fn_detect_button_conflict hasn't flagged as a conflict, or the first tap in what becomes a conflict, whose row only gets created once the 2nd tap arrives) would get sent to OpenAI to classify its own display text as free-form intent, creating a second reply_intents row for the same record that ReplyClassification:SupersedeOlder could then use to bury the real conflict/button-driven row under an AI guess. Checks both message_type (the normalized column, reliable for every row captured after add_whatsapp_button_capture.sql) and raw->>'type' (catches any pre-Phase-1 historical button/interactive row still sitting unclassified with message_type NULL) so this holds regardless of when the row was captured. Phase 6 enablement (2026-08-14): FetchUnclassified now also filters on @Categories (an array param - see appsettings.json's Automation:ReplyClassification:Categories, defaulting to just Finance) so the plan's recommended rollout (one category first, watch real classifications manually, then expand) is enforced at the query level, not just a manual promise - adding Purchase/Inventory later is an appsettings edit (reloadOnChange, no redeploy) once Finance's output has been reviewed, not a code change.
ReplyClassification.FetchUnclassified:
SELECT im.id AS inbound_message_id,
       im.channel,
       im.body_text,
       im.matched_record_id,
       ar.category_name,
       ar.natural_key,
       ar.day_overdue,
       ar.business_data
FROM inbound_messages im
JOIN automation_records ar ON ar.id = im.matched_record_id
WHERE im.processing_status IN ('matched','ambiguous')
  AND im.is_auto_reply = false
  AND im.message_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'button'
  AND im.message_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'list'
  AND COALESCE(im.raw->>'type', '') NOT IN ('button', 'interactive')
  AND ar.category_name = ANY(@Categories)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM reply_intents ri WHERE ri.inbound_message_id = im.id
  )
ORDER BY im.received_at ASC
LIMIT 20
ReplyClassification.UpsertIntent:
INSERT INTO reply_intents
  (inbound_message_id, matched_record_id, intent, promised_date, promised_amount,
   confidence, llm_model, llm_raw, status_id)
VALUES
  (@InboundMessageId, @MatchedRecordId, @Intent, @PromisedDate, @PromisedAmount,
   @Confidence, @LlmModel, @LlmRaw::jsonb,
   (SELECT id FROM reply_status WHERE status_name = 'human_approval'))
ON CONFLICT (inbound_message_id) DO UPDATE SET
   intent = EXCLUDED.intent, promised_date = EXCLUDED.promised_date,
   promised_amount = EXCLUDED.promised_amount, confidence = EXCLUDED.confidence,
   llm_model = EXCLUDED.llm_model, llm_raw = EXCLUDED.llm_raw
ReplyClassification.SupersedeOlder:
UPDATE reply_intents ri
SET status_id = (SELECT id FROM reply_status WHERE status_name = 'superseded')
WHERE ri.status_id = (SELECT id FROM reply_status WHERE status_name = 'human_approval')
  AND ri.matched_record_id IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM reply_intents newer
    WHERE newer.matched_record_id = ri.matched_record_id
      AND newer.id > ri.id
  )
ReplyClassification.ClaimAndNotify:
WITH pending AS (
  SELECT ri.id
  FROM reply_intents ri
  JOIN reply_status rs       ON rs.id = ri.status_id
  JOIN automation_records ar ON ar.id = ri.matched_record_id
  WHERE rs.status_name = 'human_approval'
    AND ri.push_notified_at IS NULL
    AND ar.userid IS NOT NULL
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_device d
                WHERE d.user_id = ar.userid AND d.push_token IS NOT NULL)
  ORDER BY ri.id
  FOR UPDATE OF ri SKIP LOCKED
),
claimed AS (
  UPDATE reply_intents ri
  SET push_notified_at = now()
  FROM pending p
  WHERE ri.id = p.id
    AND ri.push_notified_at IS NULL
  RETURNING ri.id, ri.intent, ri.matched_record_id
)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (c.id, d.push_token)
  c.id            AS reply_intent_id,
  c.intent,
  ar.userid       AS target_user_id,
  ar.natural_key  AS record_ref,
  COALESCE(ar.business_data->>'client_name',
           ar.business_data->>'supplier_name',
           ar.business_data->>'item_name',
           ar.natural_key, 'A customer') AS party_name,
  d.push_token,
  d.platform
FROM claimed c
JOIN automation_records ar ON ar.id = c.matched_record_id
JOIN user_device d         ON d.user_id = ar.userid
WHERE d.push_token IS NOT NULL

WhatsAppReconcile._comment: Native replacement for the retired n8n 'WF: Reconcile WhatsApp Status (Schedule)' workflow (Every 2 Minutes -> Reconcile WhatsApp Status). See SmartWorker/BackgroundServices/ReconcileWhatsAppStatusBackgroundService.cs. Same underlying function ReminderSend:Reconcile also calls inline after a send batch - this is the independent periodic safety-net call n8n ran on its own 2-minute schedule.

ReminderSend._comment: Native replacement for the retired n8n 'WF: Reminder Send (Automation) Latest' workflow (Every 1 Minute Trigger -> 2. Fetch Pending -> Loop Records -> ... -> Reconcile WhatsApp Status). See SmartWorker/BackgroundServices/ReminderSendBackgroundService.cs, which runs this same pipeline on an in-process 1-minute loop. FinalizeUpdate/FinalizeInsertLog are the exact same UPDATE automation_records / INSERT notification_log SQL n8n's 'Build Bulk Update Query' node builds (n8n did it as one multi-row VALUES statement per batch; here it's the same statement run once per record, parameterized instead of string-built - functionally identical, process_status is deliberately left untouched exactly as n8n leaves it).
ReminderSend.ClaimPending: UPDATE public.automation_records SET last_reminder_sent = now() WHERE id = ANY(@Ids) AND (last_reminder_sent IS NULL OR last_reminder_sent < now() - interval '5 minutes') RETURNING id
ReminderSend.FinalizeUpdate:
UPDATE public.automation_records
SET whatsapp_status = @WhatsappStatus,
    whatsapp_message_id = @WhatsappMessageId,
    email_status = @EmailStatus,
    email_message_id = @EmailMessageId,
    email_thread_id = @EmailThreadId,
    send_status_updated_at = now(),
    last_rule_sent = CASE WHEN @WhatsappStatus = 'sent' OR @EmailStatus = 'sent' THEN @RuleName ELSE last_rule_sent END,
    last_reminder_sent = CASE WHEN @WhatsappStatus = 'sent' OR @EmailStatus = 'sent' THEN now() ELSE last_reminder_sent END,
    reminder_count = CASE WHEN @WhatsappStatus = 'sent' OR @EmailStatus = 'sent' THEN COALESCE(reminder_count, 0) + 1 ELSE reminder_count END
WHERE id = @Id
ReminderSend.FinalizeInsertLog:
INSERT INTO notification_log (
  record_id, matchingruleid, skip_days, last_rule_sent, last_reminder_sent,
  due_date, day_overdue, pause_reminders,
  category_name, natural_key, invoice_ref, rule_name,
  email_recipient, email_subject, email_body, email_status, email_message_id,
  whatsapp_recipient, whatsapp_body, whatsapp_status, whatsapp_message_id
)
SELECT
  ar.id, ar.matchingruleid, ar.skip_days, ar.last_rule_sent, ar.last_reminder_sent,
  ar.due_date, ar.day_overdue, ar.pause_reminders,
  @CategoryName, ar.natural_key,
  COALESCE(ar.business_data->>'invoice_number', ar.business_data->>'purchase_id',
           ar.business_data->>'production_order_no', ar.business_data->>'dispatch_order_no',
           ar.business_data->>'item_code'),
  @RuleName,
  CASE WHEN @EmailEnabled THEN @ClientEmail END,
  CASE WHEN @EmailEnabled THEN @EmailSubject END,
  CASE WHEN @EmailEnabled THEN @EmailBody END,
  CASE WHEN @EmailEnabled THEN ar.email_status END,
  CASE WHEN @EmailEnabled THEN ar.email_message_id END,
  CASE WHEN @WhatsappEnabled THEN @ClientPhone END,
  CASE WHEN @WhatsappEnabled THEN @WhatsappBody END,
  CASE WHEN @WhatsappEnabled THEN ar.whatsapp_status END,
  CASE WHEN @WhatsappEnabled THEN ar.whatsapp_message_id END
FROM automation_records ar
WHERE ar.id = @Id

Notifications.BlockedWhatsAppNumbers:
SELECT recipient AS "Recipient", status AS "Status", error_code AS "ErrorCode", event_ts AS "EventTs", received_at AS "ReceivedAt"
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (recipient)
        recipient, status, error_code, event_ts, received_at
    FROM whatsapp_status_events
    ORDER BY recipient, event_ts DESC, received_at DESC
) latest
WHERE status = 'failed'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM inbound_messages m
      WHERE m.from_phone IS NOT NULL
        AND regexp_replace(m.from_phone, '\D', '', 'g') = regexp_replace(latest.recipient, '\D', '', 'g')
        AND m.received_at > latest.event_ts
  )
ORDER BY event_ts DESC
Notifications._insertManualWhatsAppLog_comment: Journey panel's 'send custom WhatsApp' compose box (NotificationsService.SendCustomWhatsAppAsync) - a one-off free-text message, so it writes straight to notification_log instead of going through sp_capture_automation_notification_send (which is gated on automation_records.process_status='pending' with a matched rule, and also mutates automation_records' own status columns - wrong for a manual ad hoc send). NOT YET CONFIRMED against the live notification_log schema - if this errors (e.g. a NOT NULL column with no default that isn't listed here, such as matchingruleid), the fix is adding that column with a sensible value (NULL if nullable) to both the column list and VALUES below.
Notifications.InsertManualWhatsAppLog:
INSERT INTO notification_log
  (record_id, category_name, rule_name, whatsapp_recipient, whatsapp_body, whatsapp_status, whatsapp_message_id, sent_at)
VALUES
  (@RecordId, @CategoryName, @RuleName, @WhatsappRecipient, @WhatsappBody::jsonb, @WhatsappStatus, @WhatsappMessageId, now())
Notifications._insertManualEmailLog_comment: Journey panel's 'send custom email' compose box (NotificationsService.SendCustomEmailAsync) - logs one notification_log row per manual send, same shape sp_capture_automation_notification_send writes for the automated pipeline (email_recipient/email_subject/email_body/email_status), so it shows up in Dashboard:RecordJourney the same way. No email_message_id - EmailSendResponse (plain SMTP via System.Net.Mail) never produces one, unlike a Gmail-API send would, so that column is just left out (stays NULL) rather than passed as an always-empty parameter. rule_name comes from the category's pre-seeded 'Custom' rule (Configuration:GetManualRule) purely for attribution, same convention InsertManualWhatsAppLog uses - falls back to the literal 'Custom' in C# if that lookup fails, since (unlike WhatsApp) nothing about whether the email itself can send depends on that row existing.
Notifications.InsertManualEmailLog:
INSERT INTO notification_log
  (record_id, category_name, rule_name, email_recipient, email_subject, email_body, email_status, sent_at)
VALUES
  (@RecordId, @CategoryName, @RuleName, @EmailRecipient, @EmailSubject, @EmailBody, @EmailStatus, now())

Ingestion._comment: Native replacement for the n8n 'Generic Ingestion (All Categories) webhook' - same stored procedures, same call shapes, just invoked from the API instead of an n8n HTTP forward. See FileIngestionService.
Ingestion.GetCategoryMapping: SELECT DISTINCT category_name AS "CategoryName", sheet_name AS "SheetName" FROM category_field_mapping ORDER BY category_name
Ingestion.InsertFileTracking: INSERT INTO file_tracking (file_name, created_date, file_status, status, userid) VALUES (@FileName, @CreatedDate, 'true', 'new', @UserId) RETURNING id
Ingestion.MarkDuplicates:
WITH dups AS (
  SELECT id, category_name, row_number,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category_name, natural_key ORDER BY id) AS rn
  FROM automation_staging
)
UPDATE automation_staging a
SET ingest_status = 'duplicate'
FROM dups d
WHERE a.id = d.id AND d.rn > 1
  AND a.file_id = @FileId::character varying
Ingestion.MarkFileCompleted: UPDATE file_tracking SET updateddatetime = NOW(), status = 'completed' WHERE id = @FileId
Ingestion._reviewComment: Staging review gate (StagingReviewService) - runs after BulkInsertStaging/MarkDuplicates, before SyncStaging. Classifies every staged row as new/already_exist/mandatory_field/duplicate/dataissue so the user can download an Excel report and confirm before anything is promoted to automation_records.
Ingestion.GetMandatoryColumns: SELECT category_name AS "CategoryName", sheet_column_name AS "ColumnName" FROM category_field_mapping WHERE is_mandatory = true
Ingestion.GetStagingRowsForFile: SELECT id, category_name AS "CategoryName", natural_key AS "NaturalKey", row_number AS "RowNumber", business_data::text AS "BusinessDataJson", ingest_status AS "IngestStatus", branch_id AS "BranchId" FROM automation_staging WHERE file_id = @FileId AND userid = @UserId ORDER BY category_name, row_number
Ingestion.CountStagingForFile: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM automation_staging WHERE file_id = @FileId AND userid = @UserId
Ingestion.GetExistingNaturalKeys: SELECT DISTINCT category_name AS "CategoryName", natural_key AS "NaturalKey" FROM automation_records WHERE category_name = ANY(@Categories::text[]) AND branch_id = @BranchId
Ingestion.UpdateStagingRowStatus: UPDATE automation_staging SET ingest_status = @Status WHERE id = @Id
Ingestion.DeleteNonPromotableStaging: DELETE FROM automation_staging WHERE file_id = @FileId AND userid = @UserId AND ingest_status NOT IN ('new','already_exist')

MasterAuth._comment: Master/control DB only - organisation, userinfo, organisationinfo. Never run against a tenant SmartWorkerConnection. Aliases are plain lowercase (no quotes needed) - Dapper's default mapping is case-insensitive so orgid binds to OrgId, passwordhash binds to PasswordHash, etc.
MasterAuth.GetUserByEmail: SELECT id, orgid, username, email, password_hash AS passwordhash, allowedcategories, status, created_at AS createdat, updated_at AS updatedat FROM userinfo WHERE email = @Email AND status = true
MasterAuth.GetOrganisationById: SELECT id, name, company_details AS companydetails, status, created_at AS createdat, updated_at AS updatedat FROM organisation WHERE id = @OrgId AND status = true
MasterAuth.GetOrganisationInfoByOrgId: SELECT id, orgid, db_name AS dbname, connectionstring, created_at AS createdat, updated_at AS updatedat, webhookphonenumber, whatsapp_access_token AS whatsappaccesstoken, smtp_host AS smtphost, smtp_port AS smtpport, smtp_username AS smtpusername, smtp_password AS smtppassword, smtp_from_email AS smtpfromemail, smtp_from_name AS smtpfromname FROM organisationinfo WHERE orgid = @OrgId
MasterAuth.UpdateOrganisationSendCredentials: UPDATE organisationinfo SET whatsapp_access_token = COALESCE(@WhatsAppAccessToken, whatsapp_access_token), webhookphonenumber = COALESCE(@WhatsAppPhoneNumberId, webhookphonenumber), smtp_host = COALESCE(@SmtpHost, smtp_host), smtp_port = COALESCE(@SmtpPort, smtp_port), smtp_username = COALESCE(@SmtpUsername, smtp_username), smtp_password = COALESCE(@SmtpPassword, smtp_password), smtp_from_email = COALESCE(@SmtpFromEmail, smtp_from_email), smtp_from_name = COALESCE(@SmtpFromName, smtp_from_name), updated_at = now() WHERE orgid = @OrgId
MasterAuth.GetAllActiveTenantConnections: SELECT oi.orgid AS orgid, oi.connectionstring AS encryptedconnectionstring FROM organisationinfo oi JOIN organisation o ON o.id = oi.orgid WHERE o.status = true
MasterAuth.InsertOrganisation: INSERT INTO organisation (name, company_details, status) VALUES (@Name, @CompanyDetails::jsonb, true) RETURNING id
MasterAuth.InsertOrganisationInfo: INSERT INTO organisationinfo (orgid, db_name, connectionstring, webhookphonenumber) VALUES (@OrgId, @DbName, @EncryptedConnectionString, @WebhookPhoneNumber) RETURNING id
MasterAuth.InsertUserInfo: INSERT INTO userinfo (orgid, username, email, password_hash, allowedcategories, status) VALUES (@OrgId, @Username, @Email, @PasswordHash, @AllowedCategories, true) RETURNING id
MasterAuth.UpdatePassword: UPDATE userinfo SET password_hash = @PasswordHash, updated_at = now() WHERE id = @Id
MasterAuth.UpdateEmailAndUsername: UPDATE userinfo SET email = @Email, username = @Username, updated_at = now() WHERE id = @Id
MasterAuth.GetOrgIdByWebhookPhoneNumber: SELECT oi.orgid FROM organisationinfo oi JOIN organisation o ON o.id = oi.orgid WHERE oi.webhookphonenumber = @WebhookPhoneNumber AND o.status = true

WebhookInbox._comment: Fast-ack inbox for inbound Meta WhatsApp webhooks - master DB (Database/add_webhook_inbox.sql), not a tenant DB, since we don't know the tenant yet when a webhook arrives. WhatsAppWebhookController.Receive() only inserts here and returns 200 immediately; WebhookInboxDrainBackgroundService claims and processes batches out-of-band. ClaimPendingBatch claims atomically via UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) so multiple drain-worker instances can run safely.
WebhookInbox.InsertPending: INSERT INTO public.webhook_inbox (channel, raw_payload) VALUES (@Channel, @RawPayload::jsonb) RETURNING id
WebhookInbox.ClaimPendingBatch: UPDATE public.webhook_inbox SET status = 'processing', attempts = attempts + 1, claimed_at = now() WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM public.webhook_inbox WHERE status = 'pending' OR (status = 'processing' AND claimed_at < now() - interval '5 minutes') ORDER BY received_at LIMIT @BatchSize FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING id, raw_payload AS rawpayload, attempts
WebhookInbox.MarkProcessed: UPDATE public.webhook_inbox SET status = 'processed', processed_at = now() WHERE id = @Id
WebhookInbox.MarkFailed: UPDATE public.webhook_inbox SET status = CASE WHEN attempts >= @MaxAttempts THEN 'dead' ELSE 'pending' END, last_error = @Error WHERE id = @Id
WebhookInbox.DeleteExpired: DELETE FROM public.webhook_inbox WHERE (status = 'processed' AND processed_at < now() - interval '7 days') OR (status = 'dead' AND received_at < now() - interval '30 days')

ReminderSendOutbox._comment: Duplicate-prevention outbox for outbound reminder sends - master DB (Database/add_reminder_send_outbox.sql), one row per channel per due reminder. InsertPending/ClaimPendingBatch/MarkSent/MarkFailed/MarkUnknown run against the master DB via ReminderSendOutboxRepository - decide phase writes tickets (ON CONFLICT (send_window_key) DO NOTHING is the actual dedup guarantee), dispatch phase claims and resolves them. FinalizeChannelUpdate/FinalizeChannelInsertLog run against the TENANT DB instead (same connection dispatch already opened to send) - deliberately per-channel, not the combined record-level update ReminderSend:FinalizeUpdate used before the outbox existed, since two tickets for the same record can now resolve at completely different times (e.g. WhatsApp parked as 'unknown' while email already succeeded) and each needs to write its own outcome without clobbering the other channel's columns.
ReminderSendOutbox.InsertPending: INSERT INTO public.reminder_send_outbox (orgid, automation_record_id, channel, send_window_key, payload) VALUES (@OrgId, @AutomationRecordId, @Channel, @SendWindowKey, @Payload::jsonb) ON CONFLICT (send_window_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING id
ReminderSendOutbox.ClaimPendingBatch: UPDATE public.reminder_send_outbox SET status = 'in_flight', attempts = attempts + 1, claimed_at = now() WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM public.reminder_send_outbox WHERE status = 'pending' OR (status = 'in_flight' AND claimed_at < now() - interval '5 minutes') ORDER BY created_at LIMIT @BatchSize FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING id, orgid AS orgid, automation_record_id AS automationrecordid, channel, payload::text AS payload, attempts
ReminderSendOutbox.MarkSent: UPDATE public.reminder_send_outbox SET status = 'sent', sent_at = now(), provider_message_id = @ProviderMessageId WHERE id = @Id
ReminderSendOutbox.MarkFailed: UPDATE public.reminder_send_outbox SET status = 'failed', last_error = @Error WHERE id = @Id
ReminderSendOutbox.MarkUnknown: UPDATE public.reminder_send_outbox SET status = 'unknown', last_error = @Error WHERE id = @Id
ReminderSendOutbox.ResolveUnknownWhatsApp: UPDATE public.reminder_send_outbox SET status = @ResolvedStatus, provider_message_id = @ProviderMessageId, sent_at = CASE WHEN @ResolvedStatus = 'sent' THEN now() ELSE sent_at END, last_error = CASE WHEN @ResolvedStatus = 'failed' THEN @ErrorDetail ELSE last_error END WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM public.reminder_send_outbox WHERE orgid = @OrgId AND channel = 'whatsapp' AND status = 'unknown' AND payload->>'recipient' = @Recipient ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 1) RETURNING id
ReminderSendOutbox.PresumeSentEmailTickets: UPDATE public.reminder_send_outbox SET status = 'sent', sent_at = now(), last_error = COALESCE(last_error, '') || ' [auto-resolved: presumed sent after grace window with no bounce/exception]' WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM public.reminder_send_outbox WHERE channel = 'email' AND status = 'unknown' AND claimed_at < now() - (@GraceMinutes || ' minutes')::interval FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING id, orgid, automation_record_id AS automationrecordid, payload->>'rule_name' AS rulename, payload->>'category_name' AS categoryname, payload->>'recipient' AS recipient
ReminderSendOutbox.FinalizeChannelUpdate: UPDATE public.automation_records SET whatsapp_status = CASE WHEN @Channel = 'whatsapp' THEN @Status ELSE whatsapp_status END, whatsapp_message_id = CASE WHEN @Channel = 'whatsapp' THEN @MessageId ELSE whatsapp_message_id END, email_status = CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @Status ELSE email_status END, email_message_id = CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @MessageId ELSE email_message_id END, email_thread_id = CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @EmailThreadId ELSE email_thread_id END, send_status_updated_at = now(), last_rule_sent = CASE WHEN @Status = 'sent' THEN @RuleName ELSE last_rule_sent END, last_reminder_sent = CASE WHEN @Status = 'sent' THEN now() ELSE last_reminder_sent END, reminder_count = CASE WHEN @Status = 'sent' THEN COALESCE(reminder_count, 0) + 1 ELSE reminder_count END WHERE id = @Id
ReminderSendOutbox.FinalizeChannelInsertLog: INSERT INTO notification_log (record_id, matchingruleid, skip_days, last_rule_sent, last_reminder_sent, due_date, day_overdue, pause_reminders, category_name, natural_key, invoice_ref, rule_name, email_recipient, email_subject, email_body, email_status, email_message_id, whatsapp_recipient, whatsapp_body, whatsapp_status, whatsapp_message_id) SELECT ar.id, ar.matchingruleid, ar.skip_days, ar.last_rule_sent, ar.last_reminder_sent, ar.due_date, ar.day_overdue, ar.pause_reminders, @CategoryName, ar.natural_key, COALESCE(ar.business_data->>'invoice_number', ar.business_data->>'purchase_id', ar.business_data->>'production_order_no', ar.business_data->>'dispatch_order_no', ar.business_data->>'item_code'), @RuleName, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @Recipient END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @EmailSubject END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @EmailBody END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @Status END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'email' THEN @MessageId END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'whatsapp' THEN @Recipient END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'whatsapp' THEN @WhatsappBody END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'whatsapp' THEN @Status END, CASE WHEN @Channel = 'whatsapp' THEN @MessageId END FROM automation_records ar WHERE ar.id = @Id

Branch.GetBranchesForUser: SELECT b.id AS branchid, b.branch_code AS branchcode, b.branch_name AS branchname, ub.is_primary AS isprimary FROM user_branch ub JOIN branch b ON b.id = ub.branch_id WHERE ub."UserId" = @UserId AND b.is_active = true ORDER BY ub.is_primary DESC, b.branch_name
Branch.GetAllActiveBranches: SELECT id AS branchid, branch_code AS branchcode, branch_name AS branchname, false AS isprimary FROM branch WHERE is_active = true ORDER BY branch_name
Branch.GetUserRoleNameById: SELECT r."UserType" FROM "User" u JOIN "UserType" r ON r."UserTypeId" = u."UserTypeId" WHERE u."UserId" = @UserId
